title: Patient Financial Assistance Program Policy: Determining the Tier
content:
The tier at which a Patient Financial Assistance Program case is assessed is determined as follows.

## 1. Household size and annual household income

1.1 Household size follows the program's household definition.

1.2 Annual household income counts the applicant and, where spouse income is counted, a spouse or domestic partner, but never dependents, whose income is not counted.

1.3 Annual household income is taken from the most recent accepted income document. Pay stubs covering the last pay-stub period of calendar days are annualized by multiplying their total by 365 and dividing the result by the number of days in the pay-stub period. A tax return is used as filed.

*Worked figure (hypothetical stubs, pay-stub period of 30 days).* Pay stubs totalling $2400.00 for the last 30 calendar days annualize to $2400.00 multiplied by 365 and divided by 30, which is $29200.00.

## 2. Poverty-guideline figures

2.1 The poverty-guideline figures of this policy are $15650.00 for a household of one person and $5500.00 for each additional member.

## 3. Which tier applies

3.1 An income tier applies when the household's percent of the federal poverty guideline is above the lowest figure of the tier's band and at most the highest figure of that band. The Financial Assistance Full Discount band starts at zero income.

3.2 No asset test applies.

3.3 The Presumptive Eligibility Full Discount applies, without an income assessment, to an applicant with current proof of enrollment in one of the tier's qualifying programs. Documented homelessness is proved by a shelter or caseworker letter.

| Applicant presents | Tier that applies under this section |
|---|---|
| A percent of the guideline above a band's lowest figure and at most its highest figure | The income tier of that band |
| A percent of the guideline at exactly a band's lowest figure | Not that band; the band below it |
| Current proof of a qualifying enrollment | Presumptive Eligibility Full Discount, without an income assessment |

## 4. Provisions no longer in force

The following provisions of this policy are **no longer in force**; each has been superseded by the program's current basis and is not applied:

- (a) The percent of the federal poverty guideline is annual household income divided by the guideline for the household size (the guideline base for one person plus the guideline amount for each additional member), times 100, rounded to one decimal place. *No longer in force.*
- (b) When an applicant qualifies for more than one tier, the tier giving the larger total discount on the covered invoices applies; discounts of two tiers are never added together. *No longer in force.*
- (c) The Catastrophic Medical Hardship Adjustment applies when the percent of the guideline is at most its band's highest figure and the applicant's laboratory patient responsibility for the hardship window exceeds the tier's liability-cap percent of annual household income. *No longer in force.*
- (d) When documents show a different band than the one stated at intake, the case is redetermined to the documented tier before the decision. *No longer in force.*

The figures in sections 1 and 2 remain valid; only the provisions listed in this section are withdrawn.

superseded_clauses: When an applicant qualifies for more than one tier, the tier giving the larger total discount on the covered invoices applies; discounts of two tiers are never added together.
